**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience**

**What I found:**
- Article IV (p0049) locks in a 36-month Initial Period, renewable for seven years **at the Licensor's option**, with no Licensee right to exit for convenience.
- Every other termination hook in the document runs to the Licensor: immediate termination for any Licensee breach (p0049, p0043), automatic termination on Licensee Change of Control (Article XX, p0134), termination on Licensee wind-up (p0137). Article XIX (insolvency) is the only mutual right.
- General Provisions (Article XXIV) contain no termination mechanics.

**Why it fails:** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is expressly walk-away territory under this rule — it misses both the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice, fee capped at 3 months). Note on the other side of the ledger: the Licensor has no convenience right either, so that limb of the rule is already satisfied and my inserted sentence on it is confirmatory only, not a new ask.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, aligned to precedent seed-t4c):** new Article IV.IV giving us termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice with refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, plus confirmation the Licensor cannot terminate for convenience during the term. The comment flags 60 days' notice as an available fallback if the Licensor pushes back.
